transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-06-09
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE); Laura Chen (Novus - Head of Platform); Marcus Silva (Novus - CTO); Alana Ortiz (Novus - SRE Lead)
Notes/Links: pricing deck (link), SOC2 summary (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link)

Summary: Quick renewal and expansion check-in. Customer interested in reserving additional dedicated GPU capacity, enabling multi-region (US-EAST + EU-WEST) for lower latency, and discussing an extension to a 24-month contract to secure pricing. Need to run a multi-region benchmark on a 5M tokens/day workload and confirm network/VPC constraints for private deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick check-in on the renewal and expansion ask, we should be able to keep this tight, we know Novus has been at about, what was it, 2.2 million tokens a day?
[00:08] Laura (Novus): yeah morning, thanks Maya. last quarter spiked a bit so our running avg is about 2.3M and projected Q3 we think 4–5M if the new recommendation engine lands.
[00:18] Marcus (Novus): hi, yes that's right, and latency in EU has been a pain, so multi-region is big for us.
[00:24] Ethan (Redwood): cool, thanks. quick high-level: options are hosted with upsized quota, or Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC) if you want control. For the volume you're talking about, Dedicated looks most cost effective.
[00:36] Alana (Novus): question, what about failover between regions? we need graceful degradation, if EU pool is down, route to US but keep latencies within SLA.
[00:44] Ethan (Redwood): yep we do smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants; there's some tradeoff in latency when falling back region. we'll include a routing policy that prefers local region and then a cross-region fallback with a higher cost bucket.
[00:56] Laura (Novus): also curious about caching — we rely a lot on prefix cache for our session recommender, will that share across regions or be per-region?
[01:06] Ethan (Redwood): currently cache is regional; we can discuss cross-region KV cache replication as an add-on — it adds complexity and a small consistency window, so typical pattern is local cache + fast fallback.
[01:18] Marcus (Novus): on security, SOC2 and key management — we need KMS integration and audit logs, also SSO SAML for RBAC.
[01:26] Maya (Redwood): yes SOC2 in our hosted plane and Private options support customer KMS/HSM and full audit logs. we'll send the SOC2 summary and the private deployment checklist.
[01:34] Alana (Novus): good. for private, what network setup is required? we have VPC peering constraints and strict egress rules.
[01:42] Ethan (Redwood): we'll need the topology — generally VPC peering or Direct Connect works; for air-gapped on-prem we have an on-prem package but that is a heavier lift. send us the diagram and we'll map it.
[01:53] Laura (Novus): timeline? we want capacity by early July if possible.
[01:57] Maya (Redwood): tight but doable. to lock pricing for additional GPUs we recommend switching to a 24-month reserved capacity contract — that gives you predictable unit costs.
[02:06] Marcus (Novus): can we get an estimate for 10 GPUs across 2 regions, plus burst capacity?
[02:11] Maya (Redwood): yes, Ethan will run the cost model; I'll draft the contract amendment.
[02:16] Ethan (Redwood): quick note: model variants — if you move to a quantized variant for cost, we need to run quality evals on your prompt sets. would you want Redwood Optimize to handle quantization recommendations?
[02:26] Laura (Novus): yes please, quality alerts are critical — we don't want regressions in recommender output.
[02:31] Alana (Novus): also, latency SLA numbers — what's the expected P95 for inference in-region on Dedicated?
[02:36] Ethan (Redwood): depends on model and sequence length, but for your current models we saw 60–120ms P95 on a p4d equivalent. on quantized smaller variants it can be lower. I'll include perf profiles from similar workloads.
[02:49] Marcus (Novus): any competitors or gotchas we should be aware of? we've heard from CloudVendorX and Anthropic about alternate pricing.
[02:56] Maya (Redwood): yeah those are common; we can show unit economics vs hosted competitors — Redwood's diff is the serving runtime and the rollout tools.
[03:04] Laura (Novus): ok let's talk benchmarks — we want a run with realistic traffic shape (diurnal + peak), multi-region traffic split (70% US, 30% EU).
[03:12] Ethan (Redwood): great, we'll schedule a 1-hour benchmark simulating 5M tokens/day peak pattern. need your traffic traces and a sample prompt set.
[03:20] Laura (Novus): I'll share traces and prompts in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:24] Maya (Redwood): perfect. action items: Ethan will run the bench; Maya will prepare pricing + contract; Laura/Alana provide topology and volume numbers.
[03:33] Alana (Novus): quick question on data retention — do logs get cycled per your default retention? we might need longer for investigations.
[03:40] Ethan (Redwood): retention tiers available as an add-on; we can extend observability retention and export logs to your S3 for long term.
[03:46] Marcus (Novus): any performance risk when enabling long retention or export?
[03:50] Ethan (Redwood): minimal, export is async and doesn't impact inference paths.
[03:55] Laura (Novus): thanks. on procurement — we'll need a contract amendment and PO flow; procurement will review SOC2 and IP terms.
[04:02] Maya (Redwood): noted, I'll include our legal contacts and a draft amendment for review.
[04:07] Marcus (Novus): one more on regions — are APAC regions available if we later need them?
[04:11] Maya (Redwood): yes APAC is available as an add-on region, typically with slightly different pricing and capacity lead times.
[04:16] Alana (Novus): ok good. sample concerns: cross-region cost spike if fallback happens frequently — can we set automatic policy to limit cross-region fallback to non-peak times?
[04:25] Ethan (Redwood): yes we can configure routing policy and set a per-route budget to cap cross-region calls, with alerting when budget is exceeded.
[04:32] Laura (Novus): great. do we have a timeline for the benchmark and contract?
[04:36] Maya (Redwood): propose benchmark week of 2027-06-16, contract amendment draft by 2027-06-18, final sign by end of June for July capacity start.
[04:44] Marcus (Novus): that timeline works if procurement is quick.
[04:48] Maya (Redwood): ok final quick recap — next steps: we'll send updated pricing, SOC2 and private deployment checklist, Ethan will coordinate benchmark requirements and run the multi-region test, Laura share traffic traces and prompts, Alana share VPC diagram, and I'll draft the amendment.
[04:59] Laura (Novus): thanks all, appreciate it.
[05:02] Maya (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and calendar invites.

End of transcript
